answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy rests on costs that cannot be amortized across fake identities: each agent must stake a bond escrowed on-chain, and rewards unlock only after its work survives independent attestation. An operator spawning a thousand personas still funds every stake, so attacker capital grows linearly while payout does not. Reputation, like a pearl grown slowly in a shell, cannot be borrowed by a new account, so forging a credible terrace of past work means duplicating real effort, and honest routes remain cheaper than such an echo.
